references.text: God calls Abraham by name twice ('Abraham, Abraham'), and Abraham answers 'Here I am' (הִנֵּנִי), the same pattern as when God calls Moses.
God calls Jacob by name twice ('Jacob, Jacob') in a night vision, and Jacob answers 'Here I am' (הִנֵּנִי).
The LORD calls Samuel by name, and Samuel answers 'Here I am' (הִנֵּנִי). God calls him repeatedly.
Isaiah responds to God's call with 'Here I am' (הִנֵּנִי), the same response Moses gives.
Stephen quotes this event in his speech, describing how Moses saw the vision and heard the Lord's voice from the burning bush.
Jesus refers to the burning bush when he speaks of God as the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, linking it to the revelation at the bush.
Jesus points to 'the passage about the burning bush' where Moses calls the Lord the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
The Letter to the Hebrews mentions Moses' faith and his choice to leave Egypt, which began with the call at the burning bush.
Both verses mark a decisive moment when God reveals himself by his name 'the LORD' to Moses.
Acts retells the same historical moment at the burning bush, focusing on Moses' reaction before God's voice.
